title: Last Bell, 2014
logline: Sixteen years of standing across the road, Gully says, with his daughter on his shoulders. Fifteen, Wood says. He missed one. The old dog lies down in the middle of it.

panels.composition: The school at 3:05 from across the road, the bell shape, WOOD on the far sidewalk with old BARNABY, and GULLY arriving with a four-year-old on his shoulders.

image.prompt: a man with an old dog lying at his feet on a sidewalk across from a high school with a jagged sound shape at its door, a stocky man arriving with a small girl on his shoulders, black ink

panels.composition: GULLY beside him, both watching the doors.

image.prompt: two men side by side on a sidewalk watching a school's doors, one with a small girl on his shoulders, black ink

panels.composition: WOOD not looking away from the doors.

image.prompt: a thin man watching across a street with students beginning to pour out beyond, black ink

panels.composition: Students pouring past; the girl on Gully's shoulders waving at them; the old dog asleep on the sidewalk.

image.prompt: students pouring along a road while a small girl on a man's shoulders waves at them and an old dog sleeps on the sidewalk, black ink

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays
